analysis:
The PR is documentation-only: it adds one row to docs/reference/configuration.md, shown at head line 313, for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL. The variable is exact `0` to disable and defaults to on. It selects a fused causal SDPA call for eligible full-attention prompt chunks on either KV backend, except live packed paged KV. It is read once per process and is not forwarded to LaunchAgents. No executable code, wire protocol, attestation, authorization, key custody or encryption path changes in the supplied evidence, so there is no change to A-001 through A-017 or to the TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 and TB-011 boundaries, and no new trust assumption. The row documents a numerical and performance kernel selection inside the in-process inference engine (TB-007). It touches no input from the coordinator or a consumer and no authorization decision. The prefix-cache threat T-041 is also unaffected: the row does not alter the cache gate, TTL, HMAC lookup tags or scoping. The variable is process-environment only, so the local operator (ADV-001) already controls it. That is covered by TB-003 and is not a new capability.

Unverified contracts outside the supplied evidence:
1. The real behavior of the referenced AttentionV1.swift code (the fused-prefill gate) is not visible here. Its claimed exclusion of live packed paged KV and its handling of geometry and mask edge cases are unchecked.
2. The anchor `../architecture/inference.md#scheduler-and-loop-configuration` is not verified to exist.
3. The patch excerpt is truncated, though the range map says it is complete, so a changed row beyond the visible one cannot be ruled out; the diff is shown up to the CBV2_MTP row.

These are documentation-accuracy questions, not security regressions. No findings.
